# Helping your midwife find you
## A little planning now makes a big difference on the day

**Welcome from Riverside community midwives**

In the Philippines, we say the midwife is like family. That is how we want you to feel about us coming to your home: welcome, comfortable and ready to work together.

But even family sometimes need directions. Especially at 3am, in the rain, carrying gas and air.

Whether this is your first baby or you have done this before, a few simple preparations will help us find your door and bring our equipment inside quickly. You do not need a perfect house. We are coming to support you, not inspect your skirting boards.

## First things first: when to call

**Riverside home birth cover starts from 37 weeks of pregnancy. Before 37 weeks, you will need hospital care if labour starts.**

If you think labour is starting before 37 weeks, contact maternity services straight away so they can arrange assessment and hospital care. Do not wait at home for the home birth team.

**From 37 weeks, phone the Riverside birth line when you think labour is starting.** You do not have to be certain before you call. We can talk through what is happening and what to do next.

Please call the birth line, **not your midwife’s personal mobile**. The birth line reaches whoever is on call. Your usual midwife may be off duty, asleep or enjoying a cup of tea while it is still hot.

**Riverside birth line: [insert number before printing or posting]**

Save the number in your phone and ask your birth partner or support person to save it too.

When you call, tell us:
- Your name and how many weeks pregnant you are.
- What is happening, including contractions, waters breaking or any concerns.
- Your full address, postcode and a phone number we can call back.
- Anything important about finding or entering your home.

**Please phone for labour advice. Do not rely on a text, WhatsApp message or Facebook post being seen.** You can send directions after speaking to us.

If you think your baby is coming right now and a midwife is not with you, or there is a life-threatening emergency, **call 999** and follow the call handler’s instructions.

## Help us find the right home

Sat nav is helpful, but it does not always know best. A postcode can take us to the wrong end of a street, the back of a building or, occasionally, somewhere selling chips.

Please check that we have your full address, including:
- House number or house name.
- Street name and postcode.
- Flat number and building name, if you have them.
- The entrance we should use.

If your home has a name rather than a number, tell us what is next door or opposite. “Rosemary Cottage” is much easier to find with “the blue door beside number 26”.

Make sure your house number or name can be seen from the street. Check whether a hedge, bin or parked car is hiding it.

A simple marker can help too. One family put balloons on their gate, and we found them straight away. A bright ribbon or sign can do the same job. Just tell us what to look for, and keep it clear of the entrance.

## Flats, gates and entrances: give us the inside story

Flat numbers do not always follow the order we expect. Flat 14 may be nowhere near flat 13. It may be in another building entirely.

If you live in a flat, please tell us:
- Which block and entrance to use.
- What name or number is on the buzzer.
- Your floor and whether there is a working lift.
- Any entry code or locked gate.
- Whether the entrance is around the back or on another road.

Tell us if the intercom is broken or your phone signal is poor, so we can agree how to reach you.

A **what3words location or a WhatsApp location pin sent to the birth line phone** can help us find the entrance. Please send it alongside your full address, not instead of it. Check that the pin marks the door we need, rather than the middle of the building.

Keep addresses, entry codes and location pins private. Please do not put them in the Facebook group.

## Two midwives, usually two cars

Two midwives come for the birth, usually in separate cars. **If possible, arrange two nearby parking spaces.**

We bring quite a lot: gas and air cylinders, a large equipment bag and sometimes pool equipment. A short, clear route from the car to your door makes a real difference to our arms.

If you live in a permit zone, including parts of Anfield and Kensington, check the parking rules before your due date. Ask the council about visitor permits and how to use them. Some permits need to be activated online; others must be displayed in the visiting car.

Have any permit ready and tell us where we can park legally. Please do not assume a midwife’s car is exempt from parking restrictions.

If you cannot arrange spaces, do not worry. Tell us about the nearest suitable parking and any restrictions. Nobody needs to be arguing over a parking space between contractions.

## Lights on, path clear

At night, please turn on your porch or outside light if you have one. An indoor light near the entrance can help too.

Make sure we can get through the gate and reach the door safely. If someone is available, they can watch for us and let us in. **You do not need to leave your home unlocked or go outside yourself during labour.** Agree an entry plan with us when you call.

Please clear a route through the hallway and up any stairs we will need to use. Move shoes, washing baskets, loose cables and toys out of the way.

Lego is wonderful. Under a midwife’s foot while she is carrying equipment, less so.

This is about safe access, not tidiness. The washing can wait.

## Pets: much loved, safely elsewhere

We know your pets are part of the family. Many of us love them too.

Even a friendly dog can jump up when someone arrives carrying unfamiliar equipment. Pets may also find the sounds and activity of a birth unsettling.

Please arrange a comfortable, secure space for pets away from the entrance and birth area, with someone to look after them if needed. Keep them safely out of the way while we come in and work.

We can admire them another time, when both hands are free.

---

# Fridge checklist
## Ready to welcome your midwives?

**Riverside birth line: ______________________________**

**Our full address and postcode:**

__________________________________________________

**Entrance, parking or other useful details:**

__________________________________________________

### Before your due date
☐ Save the birth line number in your phone and your support person’s phone.  
☐ Check we have your full address and any special directions.  
☐ Check your house number or name is visible.  
☐ Plan parking for two cars if possible.  
☐ Arrange visitor permits if needed.  
☐ Plan how we will get through gates and locked entrances.  
☐ Arrange somewhere safe for pets.

### When labour starts
☐ Phone the Riverside birth line — not a personal mobile.  
☐ Remind us about access, parking and entry codes.  
☐ Send a location pin or what3words location if helpful.  
☐ Switch on the entrance light at night.  
☐ Clear the path, hallway and stairs.  
☐ Settle pets safely away from the birth area.  
☐ Have someone let us in, if possible.

**Before 37 weeks: contact maternity services straight away if labour may be starting — you will need hospital care.**

**Baby coming now without a midwife there, or a life-threatening emergency? Call 999.**

A little help finding the door means we can get to the important part sooner: looking after you and your baby.
